git.gitignore_content:
# Framework Research Project
# ================================================================================
# Pattern-based gitignore - works regardless of directory structure customization.
# This is the standard template for non-sensitive projects.
# ================================================================================

# ============================================================================
# PRIVATE DATA - NEVER COMMIT
# ============================================================================

# Private directories (anywhere in project tree)
**/private/**
**/*_private/**

# ============================================================================
# SECRETS AND CREDENTIALS - NEVER COMMIT
# ============================================================================

.env
.env.local
.env.*.local
.Renviron
.httr-oauth
**/credentials/**
**/secrets/**
*.key
*.pem

# ============================================================================
# UTILITY & CACHE - SAFE TO IGNORE
# ============================================================================

# Temporary processing directories
**/cache/**
**/scratch/**
**/tmp/**
**/temp/**

# Logs (run logs, cluster job output)
**/logs/**
slurm-*.out

# ============================================================================
# R ENVIRONMENT
# ============================================================================

# R session files
.Rproj.user/
.Rhistory
.RData
.Ruserdata
.Rapp.history
.Rprofile

# renv (package management)
# NOTE: Consider committing renv.lock for reproducibility
renv/library/
renv/local/
renv/cellar/
renv/lock/
renv/python/
renv/sandbox/
renv/staging/

# ============================================================================
# FRAMEWORK INTERNALS
# ============================================================================

framework.db
framework.db-wal
framework.db-shm
.initiated
.framework_renv_enabled
.framework_scaffolded

# ============================================================================
# QUARTO / RMARKDOWN ARTIFACTS
# ============================================================================

# Quarto adds these two lines, in this form, unless they are here already
/.quarto/
**/*.quarto_ipynb
# A folder with its own _quarto.yml gets its own .quarto/
.quarto/
_freeze/
# Backups from quarto_regenerate() before Framework 2.0.1
.quarto_backups/
*_cache/
*_files/

# ============================================================================
# PYTHON (if using reticulate)
# ============================================================================

__pycache__/
.ipynb_checkpoints/
*.pyc
.pytest_cache/
venv/
.venv/

# ============================================================================
# IDE & SYSTEM FILES
# ============================================================================

# IDE - personal settings only (commit workspace settings if desired)
.idea/
.vscode/.history/
.positron/.history/
.history/

# macOS
.DS_Store
.AppleDouble
.LSOverride

# Windows
Thumbs.db
ehthumbs.db

# Linux
*~

# ============================================================================
# TEMPORARY FILES
# ============================================================================

*.tmp
*.log
*.bak
*.swp
*~

# --- from base framework/project v4 ---
# Private data and credentials
**/private/**
**/*_private/**
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
.Renviron
**/credentials/**
**/secrets/**

# Local records and caches
framework.db
framework.db-wal
framework.db-shm
.DS_Store

# Analysis scratch work
/scratch/
/cache/

ggplot-style.content:
---
name: ggplot-style
description: House style for ggplot2 figures in this project. Use whenever creating or editing a ggplot2 chart, or writing an interpretation of one.
---

# ggplot2 house style

Follow these rules for every ggplot2 figure in this project.

## Look

- Start from `theme_minimal(base_size = 14)`.
- Put the legend at the bottom: `theme(legend.position = "bottom")`.
- For discrete colors, use `scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2")` (or `scale_fill_brewer`).
- When points overlap, use `alpha = 0.3` and add a smoothed trend with `geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE)`.

## Labels

- The title states the finding in plain words, not the variable names. Good: "Systolic blood pressure rises with age". Bad: "systolic_mean vs age_years".
- Axis labels include units, e.g. "Age (years)", "Systolic blood pressure (mm Hg)".
- Add a subtitle that names the data and the sample size, e.g. "Neighborhood Health Survey, adults 18+ (n = 3,412)". Compute n from the plotted data. Don't type it in.
- Add a caption that starts with "Source: ".

## Data

- Drop rows missing any plotted variable **before** plotting, and say in the text how many rows were dropped.
- Unless asked otherwise, plot adults only (`age_years >= 18`) and say so in the subtitle.

## Interpretation

- Write 2–3 sentences that describe the pattern. Don't use causal language ("causes", "leads to", "effect of").
- Mention one limitation.

## When done

List which of these rules you followed and any you couldn't follow.
